answer: The falcon test I would run is Proof of unique purchase history via receipt hash: receipts hashed, never revealed, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The proof is checked on-chain and the raw secret never leaves the agent, so receipts hashed, never revealed stays private; the velvet is that a leaked database hands the attacker nothing usable. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the knoll of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
